title: Crouse et al. v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC found the complaint out of order and moot after the Session dismissed all charges against three Ruling Elders, ended the judicial process, and dissolved their calls following their voluntary resignations.
first_summary: The complaint alleged unspecified errors in judicial process against three Ruling Elders. The SJC found it out of order and moot because the Session had dismissed all charges and ended the process, while the elders had voluntarily resigned and requested dissolution of their calls. With the challenged action removed and the underlying dispute settled, the SJC granted no merits relief.
summary: Three Ruling Elders complained of errors in judicial process against them. The SJC found the complaint out of order and moot because the Session had dismissed every charge and ended the process, while the elders had voluntarily resigned and requested dissolution of their calls. Because these events removed the challenged action and settled the underlying dispute, the SJC did not reach the alleged procedural errors.
